page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and custom AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors. The instance features 16 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz with a 1-to-1 thread-to-core ratio, providing a highly predictable compute environment. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB per core, and includes 950 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Network performance is anchored by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in memory and data processing tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression at 36.48 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.31 GB/sec, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score of 4380.5. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput are also strong, measuring 257.74 GB/sec and 54.77 GB/sec respectively. Standard compute benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core, fall into the average tier, as does the Redis SET performance of 48.58 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m9gd.4xlarge offers a balanced resource profile by combining dedicated ARM64 compute cores, a standard 1:4 memory-to-vCPU ratio, and high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. This configuration eliminates the need for external block storage for temporary data, optimizing resource density. The instance is well-suited for workloads such as database operations, web serving, data compression tasks, and medium-scale LLM inference, where its strong memory bandwidth and local storage can be fully leveraged.
